program.source: export function evaluate({ inputs, time }) { const g = 9.8; const u = inputs.launchSpeed; const t = time; const h = u * t - 0.5 * g * t * t; const v = u - g * t; const apexTime = u / g; const apexHeight = (u * u) / (2 * g); const heightPixels = Math.max(0, Math.min(260, h * 60)); const ballY = 320 - heightPixels; const ballX = 320; const objects = []; objects.push(sdk.axis('axis.height', { x: 220, y: 320, length: 280, orientation: 'y', min: 0, max: 4, label: 'Height', unit: 'm' })); objects.push(sdk.groundMark('ground.launch', ballX, 320, 80, 'Launch')); objects.push(sdk.circle('ball.toss', ballX, ballY, 28, { role: 'output' })); if (Math.abs(v) > 0.05) { objects.push(sdk.vector('vec.v', { x: ballX + 22, y: ballY }, { value: v, direction: 'up' }, { scale: 12, minLength: 12, label: 'v' })); } objects.push(sdk.vector('vec.a', { x: ballX - 32, y: ballY }, { value: -g, direction: 'up' }, { scale: 6, minLength: 12, label: 'a' })); let motionStateText = 'Moving up'; if (Math.abs(v) <= 0.05) { motionStateText = 'Still for an instant'; } else if (v < 0) { motionStateText = 'Moving down'; } const calloutLines = [motionStateText, 'Gravity pulls down']; objects.push(sdk.callout(ballX + 48, ballY - 20, calloutLines, { id: 'callout.toss' })); const gravityStateText = 'Gravity pulls down'; const readouts = [{ id: 'motionState', value: motionStateText }, { id: 'gravityState', value: gravityStateText }]; return { frame: { width: 640, height: 420, objects, readouts }, quantities: { launchSpeed: u, gravity: g, apexTime, apexHeight, velocity: v, height: h } }; }

manifest.title: The ball stops rising. Gravity doesn’t stop.
manifest.summary: Gravity slows the ball on the way up and speeds it up on the way down. At the top, the ball is still for an instant while gravity pulls it downward.
manifest.description: A vertical height scale shows a ball tossed upward. A blue motion arrow shows velocity, shortening as the ball rises, disappearing at the top, and pointing downward as it falls. A dashed warm gravity arrow points downward constantly. A callout beside the ball reads out its motion state and gravity pull.
manifest.instructions: Change launch speed, then press Play. At the top, playback pauses so you can inspect the arrows. Press Play again to watch the ball fall, or drag the timeline to inspect any moment.
